cards.front: Strategy: work backwards
cards.back: Start with the final answer and undo each step in reverse order, using inverse operations.
cards.say: Strategy: work backwards. Start with the final answer and undo each step in reverse order, using inverse operations.

cards.front: I think of a number, multiply by 4, subtract 6, then halve. I get 11. What was my number?
cards.say: I think of a number, multiply by four, subtract six, then halve. I get eleven. What was my number? Seven. Undo: eleven times two is twenty two, plus six is twenty eight, divided by four is seven.

cards.front: Strategy: use algebra with a letter
cards.back: Let a letter stand for the unknown, write the facts as an equation, then solve.
cards.say: Strategy: use algebra with a letter. Let a letter stand for the unknown, write the facts as an equation, then solve.

cards.front: In 5 years I will be twice as old as I was 3 years ago. How old am I?
cards.back: 11. Let my age be x: x + 5 = 2 × (x - 3), so x + 5 = 2x - 6 and x = 11.
cards.say: In five years I will be twice as old as I was three years ago. How old am I? Eleven. Let my age be x. Then x plus five equals two times x minus six, so x equals eleven.

cards.front: Strategy: use a systematic list
cards.back: List every case in order so you do not miss any or repeat any.
cards.say: Strategy: use a systematic list. List every case in order so you do not miss any or repeat any.

cards.front: How many ways can you make Rp 500 with Rp 100 and Rp 200 coins (any number of each)?
cards.back: 3 ways: 5 coins of Rp 100, or 3 of Rp 100 and 1 of Rp 200, or 1 of Rp 100 and 2 of Rp 200. (No Rp 100 coins would need 2.5 coins of Rp 200.)
cards.say: How many ways can you make five hundred rupiah with one hundred and two hundred rupiah coins? Three ways: five hundreds, or three hundreds and one two hundred, or one hundred and two two hundreds.

cards.front: Strategy: use the multiplication principle
cards.back: Count each choice, then multiply. Example: 3 shirts and 4 trousers give 3 × 4 = 12 outfits.
cards.say: Strategy: use the multiplication principle. Count each choice, then multiply. Example: three shirts and four trousers give three times four equals twelve outfits.

cards.front: How many ways can 3 children A, B and C stand in a line?
cards.back: 6. 3 × 2 × 1 = 6: ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA.
cards.say: How many ways can three children A, B and C stand in a line? six. three times two times one equals six: ABC, ACB, BAC, BCA, CAB, CBA.

cards.front: How many ways can 4 people stand in a line?
cards.say: How many ways can four people stand in a line? twenty four. four times three times two times one equals twenty four.

cards.front: 8 people each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes?
cards.say: eight people each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes? twenty eight. seven plus six plus five plus four plus three plus two plus one equals twenty eight.

cards.front: Strategy: add and take away overlaps
cards.back: Count each group, then subtract what you counted twice.
cards.say: Strategy: add and take away overlaps. Count each group, then subtract what you counted twice.

cards.front: How many numbers from 1 to 100 are multiples of 2 or 3?
cards.back: 67. Multiples of 2: 50. Multiples of 3: 33. Multiples of 6 (counted twice): 16. 50 + 33 - 16 = 67.
cards.say: How many numbers from one to one hundred are multiples of two or three? Sixty seven. Fifty multiples of two plus thirty three multiples of three, minus sixteen multiples of six counted twice.

cards.front: Strategy: use odd and even (parity)
cards.back: Odd + odd = even. Even + even = even. Odd + even = odd. Use it to prove something cannot happen.
cards.say: Strategy: use odd and even, parity. Odd plus odd equals even. Even plus even equals even. Odd plus even equals odd. Use it to prove something cannot happen.

cards.front: Can the sum of 7 odd numbers be 100?
cards.back: No. Seven odd numbers add to an odd total, and 100 is even.
cards.say: Can the sum of seven odd numbers be one hundred? No. Seven odd numbers add to an odd total, and one hundred is even.

cards.front: Strategy: find a pattern in last digits
cards.back: Last digits of powers repeat in a cycle. Find the cycle, then jump ahead.
cards.say: Strategy: find a pattern in last digits. Last digits of powers repeat in a cycle. Find the cycle, then jump ahead.

cards.front: Powers of 7 end in 7, 9, 3, 1, then repeat. What is the last digit of 7 to the power 2026?
cards.back: 9. The cycle has length 4, and 2026 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 2, so use the 2nd digit in the cycle: 9.
cards.say: Powers of seven end in seven, nine, three, one, then repeat. Last digit of seven to the power two thousand and twenty six? Nine, because two thousand and twenty six leaves remainder two over four.

cards.front: Strategy: make it simpler
cards.back: Solve a small version of the problem first, spot the pattern, then use it for the big one.
cards.say: Strategy: make it simpler. Solve a small version of the problem first, spot the pattern, then use it for the big one.

cards.back: 100. Adding the first n odd numbers gives n². There are 10 odd numbers, so 10² = 100.
cards.say: One plus three plus five and so on up to nineteen. One hundred. Adding the first n odd numbers gives n squared. There are ten odd numbers, so ten squared equals one hundred.

cards.back: 5,050. Pair 1 + 100, 2 + 99, ... Fifty pairs of 101 make 5,050.
cards.say: One plus two plus three up to one hundred. Five thousand and fifty. Pair one with one hundred, two with ninety nine, and so on. Fifty pairs of one hundred and one make five thousand and fifty.

cards.front: Three consecutive numbers add to 48. Find them.
cards.back: 15, 16, 17. The middle number is 48 ÷ 3 = 16.
cards.say: Three consecutive numbers add to forty eight. Find them. fifteen, sixteen, seventeen. The middle number is forty eight divided by three equals sixteen.

cards.front: A number leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4 and 5. Find the smallest (more than 1).
cards.say: A number leaves remainder one when divided by two, three, four and five. Find the smallest, more than one. sixty one. The LCM of two, three, four, five is sixty, and sixty plus one equals sixty one.

cards.front: Strategy: the pigeonhole idea
cards.back: If there are more items than boxes, some box must hold at least two items.
cards.say: Strategy: the pigeonhole idea. If there are more items than boxes, some box must hold at least two items.

cards.front: A drawer has 10 black and 10 white socks. How many must you take out in the dark to be sure of a matching pair?
cards.back: 3. Two socks could be different colours, but the third must match one of them.
cards.say: A drawer has ten black and ten white socks. How many must you take out in the dark to be sure of a matching pair? three. Two socks could be different colours, but the third must match one of them.

cards.front: How many paths from the top-left to the bottom-right corner of a 2 by 2 grid of squares, moving only right or down?
cards.back: 6. Right-right-down-down and the other 5 orders of two rights and two downs.
cards.say: How many paths from the top left to the bottom right corner of a two by two grid of squares, moving only right or down? Six. There are six orders of two rights and two downs.
